comparison: Both evaluate the main finding about organized vs. disorganized growth (C10, C11, C13, C36, C63, C102). OpenEval finds the evidence strongly supportive, while peer reviewers accept the observations but express concern about overstating the case, suggesting the differences may reflect kinetics rather than fundamentally different mechanisms.

Both address disorganized dMTs and protein incorporation in T. brucei long flagella (C19-C25). OpenEval finds the electron tomography data supportive with reasonable inferences. Peer reviewers accept the observations but question interpretation, suggesting delayed protein incorporation may affect assembly kinetics rather than representing a different mechanism.

Both evaluate quantitative measurements of A- and B-tubule extension differences (C26-C31). OpenEval finds the data well-supported with adequate statistical testing and sample sizes. Peer reviewers accept the findings but note the limited dataset (5 tomograms per condition) and request this caveat be stated.

Both address fixation artifacts and singlet region observations (C32-C35, C88-C90). OpenEval finds the comparative data compelling and the conclusion about fixation artifacts reasonable. Peer reviewers do not challenge these methodological findings, appearing to accept them as valid technical contributions.

Both evaluate basal plate maturation in T. brucei transition zone (C41-C49). OpenEval finds the progression from organized to diffuse structure well-documented with strong visual and quantitative evidence. Peer reviewers do not raise concerns, appearing to accept the structural observations as valid.

Both address C. reinhardtii transition zone structure (C50-C55). OpenEval finds the electron tomography data and quantitative analysis convincing, noting smaller sample size than T. brucei. Peer reviewers do not challenge these observations, appearing to accept the basket structure characterization.

Both evaluate length-dependent assembly differences (C64-C65, C97). OpenEval finds the comparative data well-documented and the inference about simultaneous vs. sequential assembly reasonable. Peer reviewers accept these observations without challenge.

Partial overlap on C67 regarding assembly differences. OpenEval supports the structural evidence for different assembly modes. Peer reviewers (R3) question whether this represents different mechanisms versus different kinetics, suggesting alternative interpretations should be discussed.

Both evaluate growth rate comparisons (C72-C74). OpenEval finds the logic sound that faster C. reinhardtii growth rules out growth rate as explanation, though notes C73 involves indirect inference. Peer reviewers accept this reasoning without challenge.

Both address detailed microtubule end morphologies (C38-C40). OpenEval finds the visual evidence from electron tomography well-documented and supportive of broader findings. Peer reviewers accept these descriptive structural observations as valid.

Both evaluate methodological choices about using dividing cells vs. pH shock regeneration (C82-C87). OpenEval finds the justification reasonable based on literature and biological reasoning. Peer reviewers express concern, explicitly requesting comment on why pH shock regeneration was not used as a standard method.

Both address CP cap observations and fixation artifacts (C88-C90). OpenEval finds the authors appropriately note they cannot disprove CP cap existence but show it doesn't appear as previously described. Peer reviewers do not challenge these findings, appearing to accept them as part of the fixation artifact observations.

Both evaluate clinical relevance and ciliopathy connections (C1-C3, C14). OpenEval finds the logic sound that understanding species-specific assembly is important for interpreting pathology, though connection is somewhat indirect. Peer reviewers like the potential link to PCD patients, indicating acceptance of medical relevance.

Both address cell biological context for C. reinhardtii (C15-C16). OpenEval finds these factual descriptions well-supported as essential background. Peer reviewers accept this reasoning but request it be made more explicit in the text that flagella within mother wall must be growing.
